clue.text: Weeks without Sabbath would, more's the pity

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as a phrase
second meaning: an old exclamation of regret

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LACK A DAY and the first half of the clue describes it literally; as one word it is an archaic cry of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackaday is an archaic interjection like alas, voicing regret just as 'more's the pity' does.

clue.text: Set directions to follow: "10,22,19 … 5,24,21 … 12,26,20!"

parts.note: the calls a film director gives on a movie set
the numbered answers are kinds of each word, so the trios list examples of each call in turn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb, arrange; it is the film set. The three groups of numbers are this puzzle's themed answers, three of each call.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional sequence of commands shouted to start filming a scene.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
What's obviously in projection of luckless hitchhiker?

definitions.text: What's obviously in projection of luckless hitchhiker?

parts.note: something that sticks out obviously, as in the idiom
one who never gets a lift, whose raised thumb would hurt from overuse

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'sticks out like a ...' covers the first half; a hitchhiker's projection is the raised thumb, made sore by bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything glaringly conspicuous, while literally naming an aching digit held out by the roadside.

clue.text: (2) What gets branch of police force together?

definitions.note: stands for 2 down, CAMERA: the answer is a kind of camera

indicators.note: the police branch gets the other word put into it, so it contains it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what unites a police department into one force.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's number in brackets points to the theme: answers marked (2) each go before 2 down, CAMERA, so this one makes a candid camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid camera is a hidden one that films people unawares, a well-known type of camera.

clue.text: This wouldn''t normally inspire foremost of actresses over an award "The Queen" has collected

definitions.note: inspire in its sense of breathing in

indicators.note: the queen has the honour gathered up next to her
only the front letter of the word actresses is used

parts.note: only its first letter is used

indicators.note: the short word is turned over, written backwards

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An award for Helen Mirren's film The Queen would not usually inspire most actresses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to 'The Queen', the 2006 film that won Helen Mirren awards. Inspire means breathe in, which an organism living without oxygen does not do.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaerobe is an organism that lives without oxygen, so it does not breathe air in.

clue.text: Migration of 26 poisoner involved in a stick up

indicators.note: the two pieces are wrapped inside the reversed words
in a down clue the words read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: 26 across is SINGLE, and a single is I, one

explanation.surface: A lone poisoner caught up in an armed hold-up as people migrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 26 gives SINGLE, which stands for the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the scattering of a people from their homeland, a mass dispersal or migration.

clue.text: One not working's gone mad cutting such as extended toward Macbeth?

definitions.note: Macbeth's imagined dagger appears with its handle toward his hand

indicators.note: the rearranged word cuts into the other, going inside it

parts.note: DUD'S, a dud being a thing that fails to work

indicators.note: the word gone is driven mad, its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: An idle character, gone mad, stabbing at a Shakespearean scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A dudgeon is an old word for a dagger hilt; Macbeth sees a dagger 'the handle toward my hand' and speaks of its 'blade and dudgeon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeons are the hilts of daggers, the part held out toward Macbeth in his vision.

clue.text: Face backward point — misguided courage!

indicators.note: the word for face is written backward, last letter first

parts.note: MUG is slang for the face

indicators.note: the letters of the word point are sent the wrong way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebuke for someone who turns their face away from a point of argument with foolish bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is spirited resourcefulness or nerve, an informal synonym for courage.

clue.text: (1 down) It's not easy to describe tour guide

definitions.note: stands for 1 down, LIGHTS: the answer is a kind of lights

indicators.note: to describe once meant to draw round, so the first word encircles the second

parts.note: an A to Z is a street-map guide book, written AZ

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tour guide is a difficult person to characterise.
explanation.walkthrough: The London A-Z is a street atlas, so a guide for a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazard lights are the flashing warning lamps on a car, a standard kind of lights.

clue.text: Nothing against artist's framing 20-page article

definitions.note: 20 is 20 down, DOUBLE, so this reads double-page article

indicators.note: the painter's name goes round the other letters like a frame

parts.note: J. M. W. Turner, the English painter

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced note about a lengthy feature with an artist and nothing to oppose it.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnover is a newspaper article that starts on one page and runs on to the next, so it fills a double page.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a turnover is a piece that continues overleaf, spread across two pages.

clue.text: (3) Act without restraint on cycle?

definitions.note: stands for 3 down, ACTION: the answer is a kind of action

indicators.note: the letters are cycled round, the front ones moving to the back

parts.note: LET RIP, to go all out

explanation.surface: A cyclist letting rip on a bike, with a nod to the tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first two letters of the phrase to its end. Triple action is a firearms and mechanics term, alongside the single and double action elsewhere in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple action names a mechanism that does three things at once, so it is a kind of action.

clue.text: Leaving question (a) about energy consumed by explosion in the lab

indicators.note: the two-part piece goes round the physics symbol
the words the lab are blown apart and their letters scattered
the inner group is eaten up inside the exploded letters

parts.note: QU, the short form of question

explanation.surface: A chemistry exam paper whose question (a) concerns energy released in a lab explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving question' looks like one phrase; leaving alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequeathal is the act of bequeathing, leaving something to someone in a will.

clue.text: Source of revenue President Bush initially accepted in European card game (covered by feature)

indicators.note: the single letter is taken into the card game

parts.note: CHIN, a feature of the face

indicators.note: the facial feature wraps round all the rest
only the first letter of the word Bush is used

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A political jibe about where George W. Bush gets his money, gambling in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Bush' reads as one name, but President belongs to the definition: the Exchequer was the revenue court and its presiding judge was the Chief Baron.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chief Baron presided over the Court of Exchequer, the body handling the Crown's revenue.

clue.text: Join up with kind up-and-coming conductors

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards
this word also comes upwards, read in reverse

explanation.surface: Promising young orchestra conductors join up with a friendly group.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is an eminent musician, the usual title for an orchestra's conductor.

clue.text: It's burnt half the common people, suffering?

parts.note: RAFF, the second half of riffraff

explanation.surface: An outraged cry that half the populace has been set on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks you to picture the common people in pain: the second piece sits inside the first. Riffraff is a scornful word for the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is a fuel oil, a thing that is burnt in heaters and lamps.

clue.text: Pain for one in test of windpipe

indicators.note: the pain stands in for the one, replacing it

explanation.surface: Pain counts as one of the symptoms in a throat examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain for one' looks like an example (pain, say); it is an instruction to swap one letter for the pain word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracheal is the adjective for the trachea, the medical name for the windpipe.

clue.text: In great demand, making up a Marmite roll

indicators.note: the letters are rolled about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Marmite roll, a sandwich spread with the British yeast paste, is so popular it is selling out.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a salty yeast-extract spread popular in Britain. 'Making' only links the definition to the wordplay; the 'up' belongs in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at a premium is scarce and sought after, so it is in great demand.

clue.text: (1 down) Refreshing sorbet

definitions.note: stands for 1 down, LIGHTS: the answer is a kind of lights

indicators.note: the word sorbet is freshened up, remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A cooling sorbet described as refreshing.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobe lights flash rapidly on and off, a familiar kind of lighting at clubs and on stage.

clue.text: (3) State payment in itself?

definitions.note: stands for 3 down, ACTION: the answer is a kind of action

indicators.note: one state payment sits inside the other

parts.note: UB, unemployment benefit, another state payment

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a welfare payment contained within itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment pay; UB is short for unemployment benefit, so a state payment really does go inside a state payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Double action describes a gun whose trigger both cocks and fires it, a kind of action.

clue.text: (2)In this way, get up before time

definitions.note: stands for 2 down, CAMERA: the answer is a kind of camera

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes in the short word
in a down clue the pieces get up, read upwards and so backwards

explanation.surface: Advice to rise early, done in a certain manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo camera has two lenses side by side to take three-dimensional pictures, a type of camera.

clue.text: (1 down) Attention given in little educational establishment

definitions.note: stands for 1 down, LIGHTS: the answer is a kind of lights

indicators.note: the attention is given into the school, placed inside it

parts.note: SCH, the short form of school
EAR, as in lend an ear

explanation.surface: A note on how attention is paid in a small school.
explanation.definitionFit: Searchlights are powerful swivelling beams used to sweep the sky or ground, a familiar kind of lights.

clue.text: Not the initial letters before 1 down out

definitions.note: 1 down is LIGHTS, so this reads before lights out

explanation.surface: A late-night mail delivery, the final letters dropped through the door before bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British army the Last Post is the bugle call sounded at the end of the day, before the call for lights out.
explanation.definitionFit: This military bugle call marks the close of the day, coming just ahead of the order to extinguish lamps.

clue.text: (2) Fairy turns into king

definitions.note: stands for 2 down, CAMERA: the answer is a kind of camera

indicators.note: the reversed fairy goes inside the king
the fairy's name turns round, read backwards

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale transformation in which a sprite becomes a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex camera uses a mirror to show the photographer the exact image, as in an SLR.

clue.text: Finish off the highwayman I beat

definitions.note: the answer is something that would say this of itself, one that throbs

indicators.note: the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
ROBBER, as a highwayman robs travellers

explanation.surface: A boast from someone who has finished off a highwayman in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' looks like the definition, kill; here it trims the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A throbber is a thing that pulses, so it could say of itself that it beats, like a heart.

clue.text: (3) What''s trapped by condensing lens

definitions.note: stands for 3 down, ACTION: the answer is a kind of action

indicators.note: the answer sits caught inside the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A question of optics: what does a focusing lens capture?
explanation.walkthrough: The lens words suit the film-set theme, but the answer is concealed in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Single action describes a firearm cocked by hand before each shot, a standard kind of action.

clue.text: Voice embodies comeback of actor — his Cindy?

definitions.note: the actor's Cindy is his other half; the question mark flags the example

indicators.note: the voice takes the other part into its body
the actor's name comes back, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A singer impersonating a film star in front of his wife Cindy.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Gere was married to the model Cindy Crawford; 'his' points back to that actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is one's second self or closest companion, so a spouse can be called that.
